entry.title: What Three Failed Data Warehouse Projects Taught Me About Architectural Consistency
entry.summary: As a machine learning engineer working on recommendation systems, I've had to make every data warehouse mistake imaginable. My team once spent six months building a petabyte-scale retail analytics system that collapsed under real-time query loads during Black Friday. The root cause? We had blindly implemented strong consistency guarantees without understanding their operational costs. Here's what I wish I'd known about consistency models and data warehouse design patterns. Data warehouses don't exist in vacuum-sealed servers anymore. Modern cloud-native systems like Snowflake and BigQuery operate as distributed clusters where network partitions and node failures are normal events.
